subject: plot range too large in interactive markdown

messages.author: 9a1df0588d0145d9
messages.subject: plot range too large in interactive markdown
parts:
I know there have been previous posts on this subject, and I've tried the various solutions with some success. But I was hoping someone could explain to me what's going on with the plot range error message in an interactive markdown document. From within RStudio, the available space is determined by the plot pane dimensions. But I'm not clear what my limits are when I render the markdown document as html or as part of a Shiny app. For a particular graphic, for example, I can create an image up to 5.5" in height (par(pin=...)). Increase this to 5.6 inches, and I get the error message. Where is this limit determined?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 9a1df0588d0145d9
messages.subject: Re: plot range too large in interactive markdown
parts:
Thanks, Joe: I appreciate your prompt reply .

I previously had no luck with fig.width and fig.height in either the chunk header or knitr::opts_chunk$set. As you suggested, I just tried varying out.width and out.height with pretty much the same result. 

I should mention that I need to fix the dimensions of the plot as I need to include a rasterImage as a plot background, which I need to be readable. But I don't think the rasterImage is part of the problem, as I get the same error when I comment out the background step i.e. if I just try to create an plot with specific dimensions.

Interestingly, if I change the device to png() or pdf() then I can create a figure (on disk) of the required dimensions. I'm just not sure where the device dimensions come from for the web rendition, though I did see someone speculate in an earlier post that this problem could be remedied by manually finding the div 'main-container' in the generated CSS and changing it's max.width property. For many reasons, I was hoping to avoid that approach :). 

Atul
